project.title: The Last Ember
project.description: When the sacred fire begins to die, a mapmaker must decide whether saving the kingdom means betraying it.

characters.bio: Elegant, severe, and impossible to read. Cassian keeps the kingdom functional by making choices nobody will thank him for.
characters.name: Lord Cassian Vey
characters.notes:
Portrait prompt: Fantasy portrait of a silver-templed nobleman in black court robes, sharp eyes, candlelit intrigue, painterly realism.

Secret: He framed himself as a traitor to draw the Hollow Court into the open.

familyLinks.notes: Cassian acts as Elia's political guardian while concealing the scale of the Ember crisis.
Their Hollow Court alliance looks like partnership from the outside, but neither trusts the other.

characters.externalGoal: Seal the Ember chamber before the Hollow Court can use it.
characters.internalGoal: He framed himself as a traitor to draw the Hollow Court into the open.

scenes.title: The Impossible Map 1
scenes.content:
Rowan Vale had copied the northern border six times by candlelight, and each time the ink betrayed him.

The road to Northwatch should have bent east beyond the toll bridge. Everyone knew that. The royal surveyors had written it in green ink. The tax clerks had stamped it into their ledgers. Every trader who came through Kestrel Market complained about that miserable eastern bend as if the stones themselves had personally insulted them. But on the vellum before Rowan, the road curved west into empty mountain, toward a place the old surveys insisted had burned in the dragon war.

He held his breath and waited for the mistake to confess itself.

The archive did not help him. It creaked overhead in the midnight wind, five floors of chained atlases and rolled treaties and dead kings who had all wanted the world flattened into something obedient. Rain tapped the high glass. A mouse scratched behind the shelf of coastal soundings. Below the floor, far below the public halls and petition rooms, the Ember gave one tired pulse of heat.

Then the bell rang.

It was not loud, not at first. The Ember bell lived under the citadel, sealed behind three bronze doors, and most nights it sounded like a spoon touched gently to crystal. Rowan had heard it every dusk of his apprenticeship. It told the city that the sacred fire still burned, that bread would rise, that winter would stay in the mountains where it belonged.

Tonight the bell struck once and did not stop trembling.

The fresh ink warmed beneath Rowan's hand. He snatched his fingers back. A bead of gold appeared at the edge of the false road, bright as an eye opening in the dark. It crawled through the black line, not over it but inside it, and wherever it passed the ink changed shape. Hills unfolded. A bridge drew itself stone by stone. A river vanished under a name Rowan had never written.

Glassmere.

He knew the word. Every child in Eldermere knew it from warning songs. Glassmere was where the first firekeepers had hidden their disobedient maps. Glassmere was where dragon bones rang under the snow. Glassmere was where Oren Vale had gone before the court declared him dead and ordered his rooms sealed.

Rowan touched the vellum again.

The map answered.

A second line formed beneath the first, thin and impatient, pointing down through the citadel foundations. It pierced the throne room, the old aqueduct, the catacombs, and stopped below everything in a round chamber marked by a flame-shaped key. No surveyor had drawn that room. No royal architect had admitted it existed. Yet the map knew its name.

Ember Heart.

Footsteps crossed the corridor outside.

Rowan folded the vellum with clumsy hands, but the new road shone through three layers of parchment. Gold light spilled between his fingers. He stuffed the map under his vest, swept sand over the warm ink on the desk, and reached for the nearest harmless document just as the archive door opened.

Captain Garrick Thorn stood in the doorway with rain on his cloak and a hand on his sword.

For one stunned moment Rowan saw the boy who used to steal sugared plums from the winter kitchens, the friend who had once sworn never to become one of the king's polished blades. Then the lamplight found the captain's badge at Garrick's throat, and the old version of him disappeared.

"You are working late," Garrick said.

"Borders do not copy themselves."

"No." Garrick stepped inside. Behind him, two Ember Guard waited in the corridor. "But some of them apparently move."

Rowan felt the map pulse against his ribs.

Garrick's eyes dropped exactly far enough to notice. Not far enough to accuse. "Lord Cassian wants every northern survey delivered to Sable Hall before dawn."

"Lord Cassian can request them in writing."

"He did." Garrick held up a black-sealed order. The wax bore the chancellor's heron, elegant and predatory. "He also requested the apprentice who last handled them."

The Ember bell shuddered again below the city. This time the shelves answered. Brass map tubes rang softly in their racks. Dust slipped from old beams. Somewhere under Rowan's vest, the impossible road burned brighter.

Garrick saw the light.

The guards saw Garrick see it.

Rowan moved first. He threw the harmless document at the lamp, kicked the archive ladder into the nearest shelf, and ran before the room finished becoming fire and shouting. The map dragged heat through his blood like a hooked chain, pointing not toward any door he knew, but downward, always downward, toward the chamber beneath the throne and the truth his father had failed to burn.

loreEntries.title: Ember Magic
loreEntries.content: Fire magic drawn from the sacred Ember. It preserves, reveals, and burns lies before it burns flesh.

loreEntries.title: Living Maps
loreEntries.content: Maps that redraw themselves around hidden truths, not physical roads.

loreEntries.title: The First Firekeepers
loreEntries.content: A vanished order who bound royal authority to the Ember.

loreEntries.title: The Ember Oath
loreEntries.content: The promise every ruler swears before touching the sacred flame.

loreEntries.title: Royal Line of Marent
loreEntries.content: The ruling house that claims legitimacy from the Ember's first lighting.

loreEntries.title: Succession Law
loreEntries.content: A legal trap: the heir cannot rule if the Ember dies before coronation.

loreEntries.title: The Hollow Court
loreEntries.content: A secret court of ritualists who believe the dead should advise the living.

loreEntries.title: Circle of Glass
loreEntries.content: Mapmakers, astronomers, and oathbreakers who protect forbidden geographic magic.

loreEntries.title: Merchant Guild
loreEntries.content: A trade network that is most powerful when roads close and everyone needs boats.

loreEntries.title: The Ember Guard
loreEntries.content: The Crown's elite soldiers, sworn to protect the Ember before any individual ruler.

loreEntries.title: The Sunlit Faith
loreEntries.content: A public religion built around sunlight, truth, and carefully edited history.

loreEntries.title: Ash Rites
loreEntries.content: Funeral rituals twisted into a method for calling voices through flame.

loreEntries.title: Dragon Biology
loreEntries.content: Dragons store memory in ember-scales and can pass knowledge through heat.

loreEntries.title: The Last Drake
loreEntries.content: The official name for Nox, though the title hides more than it explains.

loreEntries.title: Speaking Trees
loreEntries.content: Ancient red pines that echo bargains made beneath their branches.

loreEntries.title: Forest Wardens
loreEntries.content: Border guardians who enforce promises made to the Whispering Wood.

loreEntries.title: River Tithes
loreEntries.content: A toll system that turns every river crossing into politics.

loreEntries.title: Embermarks
loreEntries.content: Stamped coinage whose value depends on proximity to the capital.

loreEntries.title: Market Laws
loreEntries.content: Trade rules that Rowan uses to escape soldiers in Chapter 1.

loreEntries.title: Court Etiquette
loreEntries.content: Polite rituals that disguise threats as seating arrangements.

loreEntries.title: Ember Calendar
loreEntries.content: A twelve-month calendar aligned to changes in the sacred flame.

loreEntries.title: Warning Bells
loreEntries.content: Salt-cast bells that ring before storms and, according to sailors, before treason.

loreEntries.title: Mournstone
loreEntries.content: A black mineral formed around dragon bones and used in illegal rituals.

loreEntries.title: The Cinder Road
loreEntries.content: The military road that made Eldermere a kingdom instead of a valley alliance.

loreEntries.title: The Black Winter
loreEntries.content: The winter when the Ember nearly died and the Crown erased several records.

loreEntries.title: Military Ranks
loreEntries.content: Ranks used by the Ember Guard and border keeps.

loreEntries.title: The Last Dragon War
loreEntries.content: The war everyone calls victory and no surviving witness calls just.

loreEntries.title: The Ember Trials
loreEntries.content: Tests required before coronation, originally designed to reveal corrupted heirs.

loreEntries.title: Glass Astrolabe
loreEntries.content: An instrument that projects maps of choices rather than stars.

loreEntries.title: Ash Letters
loreEntries.content: Messages written in ash that appear only when held near a dying flame.

loreEntries.title: The Ember Chamber
loreEntries.content: The sealed chamber beneath the capital where the sacred flame is housed.

loreEntries.title: Firekeeper Blood
loreEntries.content: An inherited sensitivity to the Ember's truth-revealing heat.

loreEntries.title: Glass Vows
loreEntries.content: Promises made before star-glass that cannot be spoken about directly.

loreEntries.title: River Omens
loreEntries.content: Boatfolk superstition that becomes useful when the river starts running warm.

loreEntries.title: Kingdom Borders
loreEntries.content: Political borders that living maps keep contradicting.

loreEntries.title: Red Pine Bargain
loreEntries.content: The ancient agreement that keeps armies out of the forest.

loreEntries.title: Capital Architecture
loreEntries.content: Why the city is built in rings around heat vents nobody mentions.

loreEntries.title: Noble Houses
loreEntries.content: Families whose loyalties shift according to fire, trade, and marriage prospects.

loreEntries.title: Festival of Embers
loreEntries.content: A public celebration that becomes politically dangerous when the flame fades.

loreEntries.title: Mapmaker Tools
loreEntries.content: Compasses, inks, and knives used by royal mapmakers.

loreEntries.title: Catacomb Wells
loreEntries.content: Hidden wells connecting old streets to river tunnels under the city.

loreEntries.title: Ember Sickness
loreEntries.content: A fever that affects people who survive direct contact with the sacred flame.
